result.rationale: The diff changes calendar references from a single (`.find`) to multiple (`.filter` into `calendarReference` array) and processes all of them for updates. However the merge path retains `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` — still a single `.find` — so when merging into `newBookingId`, only one old calendar event is deleted, leaving other collective hosts' events orphaned. This is a real defect exposed/introduced by the multi-reference change visible in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the code was updated to handle multiple `_calendar` references by changing `calendarReference` from a single reference to an array (`filter(...)`), and iterating them for updates. However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId)`), it still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` to select a single `oldCalendarEvent` for deletion. With the new multi-destination/collective-host behavior, this will delete only the first calendar reference and leave any other `_calendar` references (and their external events) undeleted/orphaned.
